question.text: A trader buys 10 lots of bond futures at Rs. 98.50 and sells them at Rs. 99.00. Lot size is 2000 bonds. Brokerage is 0.01% of contract value (each side). What is the approximate net profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Gross profit = (99.00 - 98.50) x 2000 x 10 = 0.50 x 20000 = Rs. 10,000. Contract value rule (pp.120, 223): buy contract value = 98.50 x 2000 x 10 = Rs. 19,70,000; sell contract value = 99.00 x 2000 x 10 = Rs. 19,80,000. Brokerage at 0.01% on each side = Rs. 197 + Rs. 198 = Rs. 395. Exact net profit = 10,000 - 395 = Rs. 9,605. The Trap: Rs. 10,000 ignores brokerage. Rs. 9,000 overestimates costs. Among the listed options, Rs. 9,604 is the nearest to the source-backed exact result of Rs. 9,605; it is selected as the closest option, not as a rounded value. Note: Always apply the contract-value formula (lots x lot size x trade price) on both buy and sell legs when computing brokerage per pages 120 and 223 of the Series IV workbook.
